answer: A new identity in an agent economy should start with nothing, like a diver dropped into an ocean with no map. To earn trust it must lock a small stake and collect attestations from established peers over time, so reputation grows slowly instead of appearing overnight. A flood of fresh accounts then faces a spiral of cost: each fake needs its own stake and its own history, and a single onyx-black record of slashing follows any identity caught cheating, making mass fakery expensive and easy to spot.
